meanings.meaning: 以奖金为报酬的拳击手
meanings.usage: 用于指当时没有规则、以奖金为目的的拳击比赛选手
形容缺乏精细规则或技术的体育项目

meanings.meaning: 丰富多彩的，引人注目的
meanings.usage: 形容人物或事件生动、引人关注
指用于保护拳手的专用手套
指专业训练或教学的机构
形容花费无度、经常欠债的行为
指接受某位老师或教练指导的人
指在大众中被喜爱或认可的程度
指对某事的结果下钱进行赌博
因债务或其他原因被关进监狱
指缺乏金钱和基本生活条件的状态
指在比赛或竞争中最优秀的人
专门从事拳击运动的人
指因某方面成就而被广泛认可

phrases.usage: 指把科学的方法或技术引入某项运动，使其更系统化

examples.en: Mendoza brought science to the game, revolutionising prizefighting.
examples.zh: 门多萨把科学带进拳击，使当时的拳击运动发生了革命性变化。

phrases.usage: 表示某人或某事在大众中极受欢迎

examples.en: Mendoza enjoyed tremendous popularity among all classes.
examples.zh: 门多萨在各阶层中都极受欢迎。

phrases.phrase: be adored by rich and poor alike
phrases.usage: 形容受到所有社会阶层人们的喜爱

examples.en: He was adored by rich and poor alike.
examples.zh: 无论是富人还是穷人，都对他崇拜不已。

phrases.usage: 指在短时间内迅速成名

examples.en: Mendoza rose to fame swiftly after a boxing match at fourteen.
examples.zh: 门多萨在十四岁时的一场拳击赛后迅速成名。

phrases.usage: 表示从友好或支持转为敌对或反对

examples.en: Humphries turned against him after Mendoza's success.
examples.zh: 在门多萨成功后，汉弗莱斯转向反对他。

phrases.phrase: settle the argument by a fight

examples.en: The argument could only be settled by a fight.
examples.zh: 这场争论只能通过一场拳赛来解决。

phrases.phrase: bet a great deal of money on
phrases.usage: 指在某人或某事上投入大量赌注

examples.en: The public bet a great deal of money on Mendoza.
examples.zh: 公众在门多萨身上下了大额赌注。

phrases.phrase: be paid as much as £100 for a single appearance
phrases.usage: 指一次出场费高达一百英镑

examples.en: He was paid as much as £100 for a single appearance.
examples.zh: 他一次出场就能得到高达一百英镑的报酬。

phrases.phrase: be sent to prison for failing to pay his debts
phrases.usage: 因未能偿还债务而被监禁

examples.en: He was sent to prison for failing to pay his debts.
examples.zh: 他因未能偿还债务而被送进监狱。

grammar.title: It was not until ... that ...（强调时间）
grammar.structure: It is/was not until + 时间/事件 + that + 主语 + 动词过去式
grammar.definition: 用于强调某事直到特定时间点才发生。结构为“It is/was not until + 时间/事件 + that + 主语 + 动词（过去式）”。 强调某个迟来的转折点，常用于叙述关键性事件的发生时刻。

examples.en: It was not until his third match in 1790 that he finally beat Humphries.
examples.zh: 直到1790年的第三场比赛，他才终于击败了汉弗莱斯。

examples.en: It was not until 1860 that gloves were introduced.
examples.zh: 直到1860年，手套才被引入拳击。

grammar.title: Though / Although + 从句（让步状语从句）
grammar.structure: Though / Although + 主语 + 动词（一般过去时）, 主句
grammar.definition: 表示“虽然/尽管”，用于引出与主句意思相反或出乎意料的情况。 用于对比两个事实，突出主句的重要性。

examples.en: Though he was technically a prizefighter, Mendoza brought science to the sport.
examples.zh: 虽然他在技术上是个奖金拳击手，门多萨却把科学带进了这项运动。

examples.en: Although boxing was crude, it was extremely popular.
examples.zh: 尽管拳击很粗糙，却极为流行。

grammar.title: Past Simple 与 Past Perfect 的时序区分
grammar.structure: Past Simple: 主语 + 动词过去式 / Past Perfect: 主语 + had + 过去分词
grammar.definition: Past Simple 用于描述已完成的具体过去动作；Past Perfect 表示在另一过去动作之前已经发生的动作，构成‘过去的过去’。 在叙述连续发生的过去事件时，先发生的动作用过去完成时，后发生的动作用一般过去时。

examples.en: Mendoza rose to fame after he had defeated many opponents.
examples.zh: 门多萨在击败许多对手后才成名。

examples.en: He founded an academy after he had become champion.
examples.zh: 他在成为冠军后才创办了学院。

patterns.pattern: The use of X was not introduced until Y.

original.en: The use of gloves was not introduced until 1860.
original.zh: 手套的使用直到1860年才被引入。

imitations.en: The use of safety helmets was not introduced until 1990.
imitations.zh: 安全头盔的使用直到1990年才被引入。

imitations.en: The practice of wearing seat belts was not introduced until the 1970s.
imitations.zh: 佩戴安全带的做法直到20世纪70年代才被引入。

original.en: It was not until his third match in 1790 that he finally beat Humphries.
original.zh: 直到1790年的第三场比赛，他才终于击败了汉弗莱斯。

imitations.en: It was not until the 20th century that women gained the right to vote.
imitations.zh: 直到20世纪，妇女才获得投票权。

imitations.en: It was not until sunrise that the fog lifted.

original.en: Though he was technically a prizefighter, Mendoza brought science to the sport.
original.zh: 虽然他在技术上是个奖金拳击手，门多萨却把科学带进了这项运动。

imitations.en: Though she was only fifteen, she mastered three languages.
imitations.zh: 虽然她只有十五岁，她已经掌握了三门语言。

imitations.en: Though the weather was terrible, the game went on.
imitations.zh: 虽然天气很差，比赛仍在进行。

original.en: He was so extravagant that he was always in debt.
original.zh: 他太奢侈了，以至于总是负债累累。

imitations.en: She was so nervous that she could not speak.
The problem was so complex that no one could solve it.
imitations.zh: 这个问题太复杂，没人能解决。

lines.en: Boxing matches were very popular in England two hundred years ago.
lines.zh: 两百年前，拳击比赛在英国非常盛行。

lines.en: In those days, boxers fought with bare fists for prize money.
lines.zh: 当时，拳击手们不戴手套，为争夺奖金而搏斗。

lines.en: Because of this, they were known as 'prizefighters'.
lines.zh: 因此，他们被称作“职业拳击手”。

lines.en: However, boxing was very crude, for these were no rules and a prizefighter could be seriously injured or even killed during a match.
lines.zh: 不过，拳击是十分野蛮的，因为当时没有任何比赛规则，职业拳击手有可能在比赛中受重伤，甚至丧命。

lines.en: One of the most colourful figures in boxing history was Daniel Mendoza, who was born in 1764.
lines.zh: 拳击史上最引人注目的人物之一是丹尼尔。

lines.en: The use of gloves was not introduced until 1860, when the Marquis of Queensberry drew up the first set of rules.
lines.zh: 门多萨，他生于1764年。1860年昆斯伯里侯爵第一次为拳击比赛制定了规则，拳击比赛这才用上了手套。

lines.en: Though he was technically a prizefighter, Mendoza did much to change crude prizefighting into a sport, for he brought science to the game.
lines.zh: 虽然门多萨严格来讲不过是个职业拳击手，但在把这种粗野的拳击变成一种体育运动方面，他作出了重大贡献。

lines.en: In this day, Mendoza enjoyed tremendous popularity.
lines.zh: 是他把科学引进了这项运动。

lines.en: He was adored by rich and poor alike.
lines.zh: 门多萨在的全盛时期深受大家欢迎，无论是富人还是穷人都对他祟拜备至。

lines.en: Mendoza rose to fame swiftly after a boxing match when he was only fourteen years old.
lines.zh: 门多萨在14岁时参加一场拳击赛后一举成名。

lines.en: This attracted the attention of Richard Humphries who was then the most eminent boxer in England.
lines.zh: 这引起当时英国拳坛名将理查德。

lines.en: He offered to train Mendoza and his young pupil was quick to learn.
lines.zh: 汉弗莱斯的注意。

lines.en: In fact, Mendoza soon became so successful that Humphries turned against him.
lines.zh: 他主动提出教授门多萨，而年少的门多萨一学就会。

lines.en: The two men quarrelled bitterly and it was clear that the argument could only be settled by a fight.
lines.zh: 事实上，门多萨不久便名声大振，致使汉弗莱斯与他反目为敌。

lines.en: A match was held at Stilton, where both men fought for an hour.
lines.zh: 两个人争吵不休，显而易见，只有较量一番才能解决问题。

lines.en: The public bet a great deal of money on Mendoza, but he was defeated.
lines.zh: 于是两人在斯蒂尔顿设下赛场，厮打了一个小时。

lines.en: Mendoza met Humphries in the ring on a later occasion and he lost for a second time.
lines.zh: 公众把大笔赌注下到了门多萨身上，但他却输了。

lines.en: It was not until his third match in 1790 that he finally beat Humphries and became Champion of England.
lines.zh: 后来，门多萨与汉弗莱斯再次在拳击场上较量，门多萨又输了一场。

lines.en: Meanwhile, he founded a highly successful Academy and even Lord Byron became one of his pupils.
lines.zh: 直到1790年他们第3次对垒，门多萨才终于击败汉弗莱斯，成了全英拳击冠军。

lines.en: He earned enormous sums of money and was paid as much as $100 for a single appear one of his pupils.
lines.zh: 同时，他建立了一所拳击学校，办得很成功，连拜伦勋爵也成了他的学生。

lines.en: He earned enormous sums of money and was paid as much as $100 for a single appearance.
lines.zh: 门多萨挣来大笔大笔的钱，一次出场费就多可达100英镑。

lines.en: Despite this, he was so extravagant that he was always in debt.
lines.zh: 尽管收入不少，但他挥霍无度，经常债台高筑。

lines.en: After he was defeated by a boxer called Gentleman Jackson, he was quickly forgotten.
lines.zh: 他在被一个叫杰克逊绅士的拳击手击败后很快被遗忘。

lines.en: He was sent to prison for failing to pay his debts and died in poverty in 1836.
lines.zh: 他因无力还债而被捕入狱，最后于1836年在贫困中死去。

questions.q: How many unsuccessful attempts did Mendoza make before becoming Champion of all England?
questions.zh: 门多萨在成为全英冠军之前经历了几次失败的较量？
questions.a: Two. He was defeated by Humphries in their first match at Stilton and lost again in their second meeting, so it was not until his third match in 1790 that he beat Humphries and became Champion of England.
questions.aZh: 两次。他与汉弗莱斯在斯蒂尔顿的首次交手中落败，第二次较量又输了，直到1790年第三次交手才击败对手，成为全英冠军。
questions.hint: 答案见课文后段：第一场被击败、第二场又输、第三场才获胜。

questions.q: Why were boxers in those days called 'prizefighters', and why was boxing considered crude?
questions.zh: 当时的拳手为何被称作“职业拳击手”？拳击为什么被认为很野蛮？
questions.a: Because they fought with bare fists for prize money, they were known as 'prizefighters'. Boxing was crude because there were no rules and a prizefighter could be seriously injured or even killed during a match.
questions.aZh: 因为他们不戴手套、为争夺奖金而搏斗，所以被称作“职业拳击手”。拳击很野蛮，因为当时没有任何规则，拳手可能在比赛中受重伤甚至丧命。
questions.hint: 见课文开头第2、4句，抓住 bare fists 与 no rules。

questions.q: What did Mendoza do to change prizefighting, and when were gloves introduced?
questions.zh: 门多萨对拳击运动做了什么改变？手套是何时引入的？
questions.a: Though technically a prizefighter, he did much to change crude prizefighting into a sport because he brought science to the game. The use of gloves was not introduced until 1860, when the Marquis of Queensberry drew up the first set of rules.
questions.aZh: 虽然他严格来说只是职业拳击手，但他把科学引入拳击，为把粗野的拳击变成一项运动作出了重大贡献。手套直到1860年昆斯伯里侯爵制定第一套规则时才被引入。
questions.hint: 见课文第6、7句，注意 not...until 1860 与 draw up。

questions.q: How popular was Mendoza in his day, and how did his life end?
questions.zh: 门多萨在全盛时期有多受欢迎？他的一生结局如何？
questions.a: In his day he enjoyed tremendous popularity and was adored by rich and poor alike. He founded a highly successful Academy, and even Lord Byron became one of his pupils. But he was so extravagant that he was always in debt; after being defeated by Gentleman Jackson he was quickly forgotten, was sent to prison for failing to pay his debts and died in poverty in 1836.
questions.aZh: 他在全盛时期极受欢迎，无论富人还是穷人都对他崇拜备至。他创办了一所非常成功的拳击学校，连拜伦勋爵也成了他的学生。但他挥霍无度，经常负债；被杰克逊绅士击败后很快被遗忘，因无力还债被捕入狱，1836年在贫困中死去。
questions.hint: 见课文后半部分，抓住 popularity, Academy, in debt, died in poverty。

questions.q: Why is Mendoza described as 'one of the most colourful figures in boxing history'?
questions.zh: 为什么门多萨被称为“拳击史上最引人注目的人物之一”？
questions.a: Because his life was full of dramatic ups and downs: he rose from a fourteen-year-old unknown to Champion of England by bringing science to the game, enjoyed tremendous popularity and great wealth, yet through extravagance fell into debt, prison and poverty. His talent, fame and tragic end make him a truly colourful figure.
questions.aZh: 因为他的一生充满戏剧性的起落：他从14岁的无名少年起步，凭把科学引入拳击而成为全英冠军，享受巨大的声望与财富，却因挥霍无度沦入债务、牢狱与贫困。他的才华、名声与悲剧结局使他成为真正引人注目的人物。
questions.hint: 需综合全文评价人物，抓住 rise to fame 与 died in poverty 的对比。

translation:
两百年前，拳击比赛在英国非常盛行。
当时，拳击手们不戴手套，为争夺奖金而搏斗。
因此，他们被称作“职业拳击手”。
不过，拳击是十分野蛮的，因为当时没有任何比赛规则，职业拳击手有可能在比赛中受重伤，甚至丧命。
拳击史上最引人注目的人物之一是丹尼尔。
门多萨，他生于1764年。
1860年昆斯伯里侯爵第一次为拳击比赛制定了规则，拳击比赛这才用上了手套。
虽然门多萨严格来讲不过是个职业拳击手，但在把这种粗野的拳击变成一种体育运动方面，他作出了重大贡献。
是他把科学引进了这项运动。
门多萨在的全盛时期深受大家欢迎，无论是富人还是穷人都对他祟拜备至。
门多萨在14岁时参加一场拳击赛后一举成名。
这引起当时英国拳坛名将理查德。
汉弗莱斯的注意。
他主动提出教授门多萨，而年少的门多萨一学就会。
事实上，门多萨不久便名声大振，致使汉弗莱斯与他反目为敌。
两个人争吵不休，显而易见，只有较量一番才能解决问题。
于是两人在斯蒂尔顿设下赛场，厮打了一个小时。
公众把大笔赌注下到了门多萨身上，但他却输了。
后来，门多萨与汉弗莱斯再次在拳击场上较量，门多萨又输了一场。
直到1790年他们第3次对垒，门多萨才终于击败汉弗莱斯，成了全英拳击冠军。
同时，他建立了一所拳击学校，办得很成功，连拜伦勋爵也成了他的学生。
门多萨挣来大笔大笔的钱，一次出场费就多可达100英镑。
尽管收入不少，但他挥霍无度，经常债台高筑。
他在被一个叫杰克逊绅士的拳击手击败后很快被遗忘。
他因无力还债而被捕入狱，最后于1836年在贫困中死去。
title: Daniel Mendoza
subtitle: 丹尼尔·门多萨

lead.question: 门多萨在成为全英拳击冠军之前，总共经历了几次失败的较量？
lead.warmup: 两百年前，拳击风靡英国，拳手赤手空拳为奖金搏斗，被称作职业拳击手，比赛粗野且毫无规则。本文将带您认识拳击史上最引人注目的人物之一丹尼尔·门多萨，看他如何把科学引入拳坛，将粗野的搏斗变成一项运动，又如何在声望与财富的顶峰坠入债务与贫困。读前请思考：他的冠军之路是否一帆风顺？
goals: 掌握 boxer, prizefighter, bare fists, science, popularity, crude, draw up 等本课核心词汇。
理解并运用 be known as, change...into..., bring...to..., rise to fame, be in debt 等固定搭配。
掌握 not...until 结构及其强调句形式 It was not until...that...。
读懂门多萨由盛转衰的一生，体会 rich and poor alike 等生动表达。
lead.summary: 两百年前拳击在英国盛行，拳手赤手空拳为奖金而战，规则全无，十分粗野。门多萨生于1764年，14岁一战成名，引起名将汉弗莱斯的注意并拜其为师。后两人反目，他两度落败，直到1790年第三次交手才击败对手，成为全英冠军。他把科学引入拳坛，广受欢迎，还开办拳校。但他挥霍无度，负债入狱，1836年贫困而终。
lead.tips: 注意 not...until 与其强调句的互换："The use of gloves was not introduced until 1860" 可改写为 "It was not until 1860 that the use of gloves was introduced"，含义不变，切勿漏掉否定词 not。

exercises.q: 汉译英：拳击手们赤手空拳为奖金而搏斗，因此被称作“职业拳击手”。
exercises.a: Boxers fought with bare fists for prize money, so they were known as 'prizefighters'.
exercises.note: be known as 表“被称作”。

exercises.q: 句型转换：用强调句改写 “The use of gloves was not introduced until 1860.”
exercises.a: It was not until 1860 that the use of gloves was introduced.
exercises.note: not...until 改 It was not until...that...。

exercises.q: 填空：Though he was technically a prizefighter, Mendoza did much to change crude prizefighting ____ a sport, for he brought science ____ the game.
改错：Mendoza rose to fame swift after a boxing match when he was only fourteen years old.
exercises.note: 副词 swiftly 修饰动词 rise。

exercises.q: 汉译英：他在全盛时期极受欢迎，无论富人还是穷人都对他崇拜备至。
exercises.a: In his day he enjoyed tremendous popularity and was adored by rich and poor alike.
exercises.note: in his day / rich and poor alike。

exercises.q: 填空（时态）：Boxing ____ (change) a great deal since Mendoza's day.
exercises.note: since 引导，用现在完成时。

exercises.q: 填空（比较级）：Mendoza earned ____ (much) money than most prizefighters of his day.

quiz.q: 两百年前的拳击手为何被称作 “prizefighters”？
options: They trained hard for the prize.
They fought with bare fists for prize money.
They were paid by the Marquis of Queensberry.
They fought only for fame and honour.
quiz.note: 为奖金赤手搏斗，故称 prizefighter。

quiz.q: 昆斯伯里侯爵的第一套拳击规则制定于哪一年？
quiz.note: 1860年 draw up 第一套规则。

quiz.q: 门多萨对拳击运动最重要的贡献是什么？
options: He invented the boxing gloves.
He became Champion of England.
He brought science to the game.
He founded a highly successful Academy.

quiz.q: 门多萨与汉弗莱斯交手几次才获胜？
options: He won at the first match.
He won at the second match.
He won at the third match in 1790.
He never beat Humphries.

quiz.q: 下列哪一句正确描述了门多萨的财务状况？
options: He died rich and famous.
He was so extravagant that he was always in debt.
He gave all his money to Lord Byron.
He earned nothing from his Academy.
Only the rich liked him.
Only the poor liked him.
Both the rich and the poor liked him.
Neither the rich nor the poor liked him.
